title: Affine base change for Hom out of a perfect complex
statement: Consider a cartesian square of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes X'=X\times_S S' with g_X:X'\to X, f:X\to S, and g:S'\to S [def-pc-fibre-product], where S=\operatorname{Spec}(R) and S'=\operatorname{Spec}(R') are affine and f and g are Tor independent, meaning that for all x\in X and s'\in S' with the same image s\in S one has \operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathcal O_{S,s}}(\mathcal O_{X,x},\mathcal O_{S',s'})=0 for all i>0. If M is a perfect complex on X [def-pc-perfect-complex] and K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X) [def-pc-derived-category], then the canonical comparison $$R\operatorname{Hom}_X(M,K)\mathbin{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}}R'\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(Lg_X^*M,Lg_X^*K)$$ in D(R') is an isomorphism. Here global R\operatorname{Hom} is the derived global Hom complex of [def-pc-global-derived-rhom], and the comparison is induced by derived pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback].

proof.text: Perfect M has quasi-coherent cohomology. Use the derived tensor/internal-Hom adjunction and its symmetric form in perfect_rhom_tensor_comparison. It supplies a quasi-coherent perfect dual D and an invertible comparison K tensor D → R𝓗om(M,K). Tensor symmetry gives an isomorphism e:D tensor K ≅ R𝓗om(M,K).
Apply torIndependent_perfect_tensor_baseChange to D and K, using the given Tor independence. Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of f follow from X being qcqs and the base being affine.

Prove naturality of schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap from its actual mate definition: paste the two pullback composition comparisons, the equality of the composites in the square and the direct-image counit to make a natural transformation before transposition; naturality of Adjunction.homEquiv transposes its square. Apply this square to e.hom. Since functors preserve isomorphisms, the base-change map on R𝓗om(M,K) is invertible.

Use affineGlobalHomBaseChange_factorization, which assumes no Tor independence, to express the global Hom map as the sections functor applied to this sheaf base-change map, preceded and followed by isomorphisms. A functor maps an invertible arrow to an invertible arrow; composing with the two isomorphisms proves the claim.

lean.statement: theorem affineMorphism_hom_out_of_perfect [∀ Z : Scheme.{uAH}, HasDerivedCategory.{wAH} (SheafOfModules.{uAH} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace))] [∀ (A : Type uAH) [Ring A], HasDerivedCategory.{wAH} (ModuleCat.{uAH} A)] {R B : CommRingCat.{uAH}} {X : Scheme.{uAH}} [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (f : X ⟶ Spec R) (g : Spec B ⟶ Spec R) [∀ U : X.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{wAH} (SheafOfModules.{uAH} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))] (hTor : PullbackStalkTensor.IsTorIndependent f g) (M K : schemeDerivedCategory X) (hM : Scheme.IsPerfect X M) (hK : schemeDerivedQCohProperty X K) : IsIso (affineGlobalHomBaseChangeMap f g M K hM hK)
